newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end firm on Dow, top blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end firm on Dow, top blue-chips.

text.p: Helped by firm Wall Street stock prices, Brazil shares closed strong on Friday in high turnover with top blue-chips leading the rise, brokers said.
Traders had expected a slow day ahead of Carnival holiday next week, but the bolsa gained strength as U.S. stocks and bonds rallied.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended up 2.07 percent at 83,166 points. Market volume was a high 511.3 million reais ($491.6 million).

Trade resumed after Petrobras sent a statement to the stock exchanges saying it had appealed the court order and it was not under obligation to pay the fine yet.
It also said it was unlikely to pay such a large fine.
"It appears that it will be a long legal process," said one trader, adding that players had already absorbed the news.
Petrobras' voting stock closed up 3.87 percent at 174.50 reais after surging over seven percent earlier.
Analysts said Petrobras common shares moved on continued expectations that foreign investors will be allowed to purchase the company's voting stock when a new oil law is approved by Congress.
State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce also posted sharp gains, closing at 26.10 reais, up 4.61 percent.
Vale stock had dropped on Thursday as traders were disappointed with news that bid specifications for Vale's selloff would only be available in late February or early March.
But the stock rebounded as players remain optimistic about the company's privatization.
Bellwether Telebras rose 1.41 percent to 93.30 reais, increasing market expectations that Telebras at 92 real strike price will be exercised on February 17 when the options expire.
Next week, shortened by the Carnival holiday, investors will be looking at the futures index settlement Thursday and the last sessions before the options expiry.
Brazilian stock exchanges will close Monday and Tuesday, reopening Wednesday afternoon for a half-day session.
